title: Will Nifty cross 26,000 today? - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
With Nifty approaching 26,000, further gains will increasingly depend on earnings growth and broader sector participation rather than institutional liquidity alone. | Photo Credit: REUTERS/THOMAS PETER

Domestic markets are likely to open on strong note, indicates trading at Gift Nifty. Sustained foreign portfolio inflows, backed by steady domestic institutional support, have set Indian stock markets up for a strong phase.

Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO of HST Wealth, said, Indian equities continue to benefit from a shift in global capital allocation away from AI-linked investments towards domestic growth-oriented markets. Foreign investments into Indian equities have reached a record $14.28 billion this November, putting benchmark indices on course for their strongest monthly performance since April 2020. However, with Nifty approaching 26,000, further gains will increasingly depend on earnings growth and broader sector participation rather than institutional liquidity alone.

Gift Nifty at 26,023 indicates a gap up opening of about 100 points.

The latest US economic data released on Wednesday presents a fresh challenge. “Third-quarter GDP growth was revised sharply higher from 3.4% to 4.3% on an annualised basis, driven by stronger consumer spending and business investment. October PCE Inflation rose to 3.8%, while Core PCE Inflation increased to 3.3%, exceeding expectations of 3.2%. The combination of strong economic demand and persistent inflation strengthens the possibility of a December Fed Rate Hike. While resilient US consumption supports global demand, further monetary tightening could challenge equity valuations. India’s ability to sustain foreign inflows despite this changing policy outlook will be an important indicator of investor confidence,” he said.

Meanwhile, equites across Asian Pacific region are up, bouncing back from recent fall. Sentiment also got a lift from a sharp overnight rebound in US stocks, which opened weak but closed firm.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said: “Despite the upbeat opening signals, the rally faces several potential headwinds, including rising crude prices, geopolitical uncertainty and continued weakness in US technology stocks. The market’s ability to hold above 26,000 beyond the opening surge, alongside sustained foreign institutional inflows and continued strength in banking stocks, will be critical in determining whether the rebound gathers momentum toward fresh record highs or invites profit-booking at elevated levels.”

From a technical perspective, immediate support is placed in the 25,500–25,600 zone, while resistance is seen at 26,000–26,100, said Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking. The daily RSI has rebounded to 71.21, although it remains below its average of 75.78, indicating a recovery in momentum. Derivatives data also points towards improving sentiment, with the Put-Call Ratio (PCR) rising to 0.85. The highest Call Open Interest is concentrated at 26,000, while the highest Put Open Interest is at 25,000, with fresh Put writing observed around 25,700. India VIX settled marginally lower at 17.68.

“Bank Nifty closed at 63,703.25, advancing 1,117.90 points (+1.79%), supported by renewed buying interest in heavyweight private banking stocks. The index opened higher at 63,408.60, tested an intraday low of 63,247.90 and subsequently moved higher to touch 64,133.80 before closing with strong gains,” he said.
